expected_behavior: When an enum-valued assignment uses a bare identifier that is present in the local type environment, the identifier must remain a variable reference even if its name matches an enum member. Enum-member flattening applies only to unbound identifiers, allowing normal type checking to reject an incompatible shadowing variable.
fix_patch:
diff --git a/rust/fsl-core/src/domain.rs b/rust/fsl-core/src/domain.rs
--- a/rust/fsl-core/src/domain.rs
+++ b/rust/fsl-core/src/domain.rs
@@ -333,6 +333,7 @@ fn normalize(
             && output
                 .chars()
                 .all(|character| character.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || character == '_')
+            && !type_env.contains_key(&output)
         {
             output = self.enum_value(target, &output);
         }
